observations.text: FIPS 203 specifies ML-KEM for shared-secret establishment and describes security as a present belief tied to a computational problem.
observations.locator: Abstract; KEM definition and security paragraphs
observations.limitations: Standard-level statement does not validate a particular deployment or product.

observations.text: FIPS 204 specifies ML-DSA for digital-signature generation and verification.
observations.limitations: Algorithm function is not deployment assurance.

observations.text: FIPS 205 specifies the hash-based SLH-DSA signature algorithm.
observations.limitations: Algorithm function is not deployment assurance.

observations.text: NSA explains that QKD requires source authentication and specialized equipment, and practical assurance depends on engineering.
observations.limitations: Government NSS guidance is not a universal ban or complete research comparison of every QKD design.

observations.text: NCCoE separates cryptographic discovery/risk prioritization from interoperability testing.
observations.limitations: Framework inspiration; the synthetic model is not a NIST-prescribed scoring algorithm.

observations.text: The cited QuSecure page reports a product-leadership award and describes orchestration/crypto-agility in its vendor release.
observations.locator: Dated release body; 2024 award and QuProtect paragraphs
observations.limitations: Vendor statements are not independent evidence of performance, government authorization or student interaction.

observations.text: Quranium describes DeQUIP as a category/alliance it invites organizations to help establish.
observations.limitations: Current marketing description does not substantiate Layer-2 architecture or unconditional security.

observations.text: The deterministic run emits 15 rows for 5 synthetic assets under 3 hypothetical horizons; A-001 triggers at 5 and 10 years and has +2 years slack at 20.
observations.limitations: Illustrative input assumptions; no forecast, live measurement or vendor comparison.

claims.text: The presentation provides a conceptual starting point for a PQC inquiry, not evidence of a completed PQC implementation.
claims.reasoning: Its extracted text presents definitions, motivations and company examples, without a documented implementation method or measurements.
claims.counterargument: Visual content or speaker notes not captured by text extraction could contain additional evidence.
claims.limitation: Conclusion is limited to extracted text; student authorship and attendance remain unverified.

claims.text: Replace blanket security language with conditional resistance and explicitly separate algorithm choice from system assurance.

source_locators.locator: Abstract; KEM definition and security paragraphs

claims.reasoning: The deck uses unconditional phrasing, whereas the standard describes a computational assumption and present security belief.
claims.counterargument: Short introductory slides often simplify to make an idea understandable.
claims.limitation: This audit does not prove any attack or validate an implementation.

claims.text: A migration comparison must separate key establishment from digital signatures.

source_locators.locator: Abstract; KEM definition and security paragraphs

claims.reasoning: The standards have different functions; a signature algorithm cannot simply replace a key-establishment mechanism.
claims.counterargument: A high-level presentation can group all these under PQC for introduction.
claims.limitation: Protocol integration, parameter choice and implementation review are outside this code demonstration.

claims.text: The PQC-versus-QKD slide should compare functions, authentication and infrastructure assumptions rather than rank either as inherently secure.
claims.reasoning: The distinction is useful but insufficient for whole-system assurance; QKD still needs authenticated origins and engineered components.
claims.counterargument: Specialized QKD research may address particular constraints in particular deployments.
claims.limitation: No QKD device or channel has been tested; NSA context is identified rather than generalized.

claims.text: QuSecure and Quranium should be treated as differently scoped vendor case studies, without an evidence-backed winner.

source_locators.locator: Dated release body; 2024 award and QuProtect paragraphs

claims.reasoning: The supplied deck and vendor sources do not offer comparable independently measured endpoints; a branding category is not certification.
claims.counterargument: A vendor may have nonpublic audits, deployment documents or later technical evidence.
claims.limitation: No inference of fraud or insecurity; the available evidence is simply insufficient to establish the broad claims.

claims.text: Add claim-level citations and quarantine the Quranium Layer-2 and guarantee statements pending architecture evidence.
claims.reasoning: The deck lacks a Quranium-specific citation; the current category page does not establish the architecture claim.
claims.counterargument: The original author might have relied on an omitted source or a contemporaneous conversation.
claims.limitation: Missing citation is an evidence gap, not proof the assertion is false.

claims.text: A synthetic inventory and timing-sensitivity exercise makes the migration question inspectable without pretending to test cryptographic security.
claims.reasoning: Inventory and interoperability are distinct migration tasks; a transparent arithmetic exercise addresses planning assumptions only.
claims.counterargument: A heuristic can conceal complexity and does not replace real discovery, protocol tests or cost analysis.
claims.limitation: The trigger equation is a repository-defined educational rule, not a NIST risk score or quantum arrival prediction.

claims.text: The long-lived synthetic archive remains a planning trigger in two short-horizon scenarios, while unknown algorithms, signatures and a PQC pilot require separate review.
claims.reasoning: A-001 has 15 years lifetime plus 3 years migration, so slack is -13,-8,+2 for horizons 5,10,20; noncomparable uses are not assigned a safety label.
claims.counterargument: Different retention needs, migration times or scenario horizons can change the result.
claims.limitation: Only synthetic arithmetic is established; positive slack is not security or permission to delay.

claims.text: A follow-up should measure compatibility and failure handling in a local, approved test environment after the student understands the evidence audit.
claims.reasoning: Interoperability addresses a different evidence gap from source reading and arithmetic.
claims.counterargument: The student may prefer source evaluation as the completed contribution and leave implementation outside scope.
claims.limitation: Proposed only; no benchmark, deployment or student completion is claimed.
